sources_considered.why: Shows that frequency in training data affects arithmetic accuracy, but for other models (GPT-J and Pile-trained models), not Minerva.
Notes that Minerva is too large and closed for outside researchers to analyse. It offers no causal evidence.

receipt.public_excerpt: Our results consistently demonstrate that models are more accurate on instances whose terms are more prevalent, in some cases above $70\%$ (absolute) more accurate on the top 10\% frequent terms in comparison to the bottom 10\%.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that arithmetic accuracy depends on training frequency in other GPT-style models, which fits the kind of explanation Marcus offers. It does not study Minerva, so it is context only.

unresolved_gaps: No study found tests Minerva's arithmetic against its training-data frequency.
Other explanations, such as how numbers are split into tokens or the length of the calculation, were not ruled out for Minerva.
